Watch out!
The digit rule changes from question to question.
QuestionWatch forExample
Q 1CAN be implied: test every option.One example that breaks a claim makes it false.
Q 2SUFFICIENT means enough to fix one password.A statement you do not need can be left out.
Q 4All the digits must be different.1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 6 is not allowed.
Q 7A swap may join digits that are not side by side.Swapping the 1st and 5th digits is one swap.
Q 10Each digit is used at least once.77777 is not allowed: it has no 1 or 5.
6
Try one first, with Dyna
Use each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once. What is the smallest 4-digit even number you can make?
a) 2047
b) 2074
c) 2470
d) 2407
Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: "4 digits, each used once, the smallest number, and it must be even."
Hint 2 · Vault
What do you know? A number cannot start with 0, and an even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
Hint 3 · Slicer
Fill one place at a time. Pick the smallest digit allowed in the first place, then the smallest for the next place.
YOUR TURN
Two digits are left. Which order keeps the number even and as small as possible?
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
There is no activity in this chapter. Keep a sheet ready to write numbers in place-value boxes, from ten thousands to ones.
Challenge ahead
The Thinking Spot is a stacking puzzle: four shapes, four friends and two clues. Keep your starting routine ready!
